text:
maria: heads-up — ACME (acct 8421) reporting 401s from their background worker after we rotated keys last night. they say dashboard shows an active key but their service fails.

acme-customer: reproducer — simple curl, from their CI:```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Token rwd_3f2b-1a2b-3c4d-5e6f-7g8h" https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
```

acme-customer: response:```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"authentication failed","detail":"key malformed or expired"}
```

alex: thanks. couple of quick checks: did they copy the key from a PDF/email? what header format did they use in other places (dashboard vs CI)?

acme-customer: copied from a PDF our SSO system emailed. dashboard console shows the key when they click reveal and it works for quick manual tests. CI uses the token above and fails.

alex: ok — two likely culprits: (1) invisible / formatting bytes introduced by PDF copy (soft hyphen, zero-width space) or (2) SSO-issued short-lived key already expired but dashboard cached the reveal. can you paste last 6 chars of the key id or the key id prefix?

acme-customer: key id ends with ...5e6f-7g8h (that's what dashboard shows).

jordan: I'll try to repro locally with a deliberately hyphenated copy. can you confirm the platform region and timeframe?

maria: region eu-west-1, rotation happened 2024-09-14 02:30 UTC, customer first saw errors ~02:45 UTC.

jordan: repro steps I used: (1) copy key from dashboard but paste into a text editor that hides soft-hyphen; (2) echo -n 'copied-string' | od -An -tx1 to reveal hidden bytes. example command I used:```
echo -n "rwd_3f2b-1a2b-3c4d-5e6f-7g8h" | od -An -tx1
```

jordan: on a machine where I pasted from a PDF the output included `c2 ad` midway (UTF-8 for SOFT HYPHEN U+00AD). server treats that as part of the token -> mismatch -> 401.

alex: that matches a class of past issues but with a twist (PDF soft-hyphen). good catch.

emily: recommended customer-facing steps to unblock: (1) copy key from Dashboard -> Reveal -> click the small "Copy plain" icon (we added this in ui v2), or use the Download key button; (2) paste into CI env using a safe method: `printf '%s' "$KEY" > /dev/null` and check `echo -n "$KEY" | od -An -tx1` to verify no odd bytes. send them the two lines to run.

acme-customer: ran od, confirmed extra byte sequence present. re-copied using Dashboard -> Download key, CI job succeeded. thanks! :white_check_mark:

jordan: mitigation notes for support: (a) mark this as "copy-formatting" class, (b) add KB link explaining PDF -> soft hyphen and how to detect with od/xxd, (c) consider showing a small hex-preview on reveal modal for support-only view.

emily: I'll open a follow-up ticket with product to add a one-click "copy as plain text" fallback (if not already present in the customer's UI version) and to add UX hint about PDF copy. tagging @product.

deploy-bot: new support-ticket created: #SUP-2024-8421 (priority: low, customer unblocked).

alex: closing thread — root cause: invisible PDF/formatting character (SOFT HYPHEN) inserted into key during copy -> token mismatch -> 401 invalid_api_key. suggested doc + small UX fix. :mag:
